question.problem: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(1\right),$ calculate $P\left(X < 2\right).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128540/assets/f3440005b2b4e7ce1cc2eed5825d11cb309522a6807bcd18ffada189fadd0cda.svg)

We're given that

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( 1 \right).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128540/assets/1f2f28b0f36aeb85a07076e1507c9561b707bf7d00de727998b02075b5458da4.svg)

Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(X < 2\right)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-x}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.8647\end{aligned}
$$
